name: Exponential decay
description:
The linear test equation dy/dt = −k·y with y(0) = y0, whose solution y0·e^(−k·t) is known exactly. It is the equation solvers are designed and analysed on (Dahlquist's test equation), and here it is the smallest compartment model there is: one compartment emptied by a first-order transfer out of the model. Exact is the closed form, worked out at every saved time, so the solver's error can be read straight off the Table: with dp45 at a relative tolerance of 1e-6, y and Exact agree to within 3e-6 after ten time constants. That global error is a little larger than the tolerance, which bounds the error of each step, not of the whole run.

The value axis is logarithmic, so the decay is a straight line.

Try: set k to 1e6. The answer is gone within a few tens of microseconds, yet dp45 still needs three million steps to cross the ten seconds, because an explicit method's step must stay below about 3.3/k to be stable, however accurate a longer one would be. The NDF solver, built for stiff problems, needs 248 steps. That gap is what stiffness means.
